position_a: Use external sidechain detection with this controlled approach: On a duplicated test route, feed a clearly different trigger into Compressor side chain, use Listen to verify the detector where available, then compare bypassed and active processing.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: ordinary volume automation or arrangement changes
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the target signal changing only when the trigger crosses the detector threshold; reject the approach if routing the trigger into the audible path, choosing the wrong source, or judging makeup gain as ducking.

position_a: Use selecting a sidechain input in Logic with this controlled approach: Solo a short representative section, choose the intended source from the plug-in Side Chain menu, then verify detector activity before changing threshold or ratio.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: route a dedicated bus or ghost trigger when direct source selection is unsuitable
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by gain reduction or gate activity following the intended source rather than the target itself; reject the approach if selecting a bus with no signal, a pre/post route that differs from expectation, or a stale renamed source.

position_a: Use kick-triggered bass ducking with this controlled approach: Route the kick to the bass compressor sidechain, start with obvious gain reduction to confirm timing, then back off threshold, ratio, attack, and release while level-matching.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: edit note lengths, change arrangement, EQ the overlap, or adjust kick/bass balance
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the kick becoming distinct while the bass returns naturally before the next important note; reject the approach if pumping, missing bass sustain, clicks, or solving a tuning/arrangement problem with ducking.

position_a: Use vocal-triggered music ducking with this controlled approach: Route the vocal or a filtered vocal bus to a music-bus compressor sidechain, begin with 1–2 dB of audible reduction, and compare in context at matched vocal loudness.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: automate selected instruments, revise arrangement, or ride the vocal
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by lyrics becoming easier to follow without the accompaniment audibly breathing; reject the approach if consonants causing chatter, low vocal notes over-triggering, or the complete mix shrinking.

position_a: Use rhythmic pumping with this controlled approach: Use a simple four-on-the-floor trigger or ghost kick, exaggerate threshold and ratio, then tune attack and release against one bar before reducing depth.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: draw volume automation or use a dedicated rhythmic modulation tool
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by a consistent musical swell that recovers at the intended subdivision; reject the approach if release fighting the tempo, transient clicks, or bass notes vanishing unpredictably.

position_a: Use ghost-trigger sidechain with this controlled approach: Create a muted/no-output MIDI or audio trigger routed to a bus visible to the sidechain, verify the bus meter and detector, then compare with the trigger disabled.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: draw automation or use the audible kick when it already provides the right rhythm
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the target ducking on the intended pattern while the trigger itself remains inaudible; reject the approach if accidentally routing the trigger to Stereo Out, losing the trigger during export, or creating hidden project complexity.

position_a: Use sidechain filtering with this controlled approach: Enable the Compressor sidechain filter and Listen, sweep frequency/Q to isolate the useful trigger component, then disable Listen and compare gain-reduction behavior.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: clean or edit the trigger, use a dedicated trigger bus, or automate the target
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by more stable triggering with fewer false reductions while the target tone stays unchanged; reject the approach if filtering out the real trigger, using a resonant filter that chatters, or confusing detector EQ with audible EQ.

position_a: Use sidechain compressor not reacting with this controlled approach: Temporarily lower threshold and raise ratio, verify the selected sidechain source and meter, use Side Chain Listen where available, then restore musical settings.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: use ordinary compression if external triggering is unnecessary
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by clear gain reduction exactly when the trigger sounds; reject the approach if leaving exaggerated settings active, listening to the wrong bus, or troubleshooting while the trigger is muted.

position_a: Use noise-gate sidechaining with this controlled approach: Select a clear trigger as Noise Gate sidechain, exaggerate threshold/range to verify the relationship, then tune attack, hold, and release on one phrase.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: manual editing, automation, or source-level cleanup
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the target opening on the intended event and closing without chopping useful tails; reject the approach if clicks, missing soft notes, shortened ambience, or bleed opening the gate.

position_a: Use stereo, latency, and sidechain timing with this controlled approach: Use a simple centered trigger, compare detector Sum/Max and Peak/RMS choices, bypass latency-heavy upstream plug-ins, and inspect whether both channels recover together.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: use linked volume automation or a simpler low-latency trigger path
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by center stability and ducking aligned with the trigger without channel image wobble; reject the approach if misdiagnosing a routing delay as attack time or breaking intentional stereo independence.

position_a: Use track versus region automation with this controlled approach: Duplicate a short region, place one test move as track automation and one as region automation, then move/loop the region and observe which data follows.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: use region gain/editing or MIDI controller data when the change belongs inside the performance
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the intended movement staying attached to the correct musical object; reject the approach if duplicating automation, leaving data behind, or overwriting a different owner.

position_a: Use word-level volume rides with this controlled approach: Show volume automation, add boundary points around the word, move the enclosed segment slightly, and compare the phrase in context.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: use region gain before compression when the imbalance should change processor input
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the word becoming intelligible without a visible or audible jump in ambience; reject the approach if over-riding breaths/consonants, creating abrupt edges, or fighting later bus processing.

position_a: Use pan automation with this controlled approach: Automate one modest left-to-right move over a duplicated section, use a smooth curve, then check speakers, headphones, and mono.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: use static panning, arrangement handoff, or send-pan automation
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by a clear musical movement that supports the transition and remains stable in mono; reject the approach if motion sickness, sudden level shifts from pan law, or confusing width with position.

position_a: Use plug-in parameter automation with this controlled approach: Choose the target plug-in parameter in the automation lane, place a small two-state move, and compare with the lane bypassed/read off.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: duplicate the plug-in for separate sections or edit the source/arrangement
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by only the intended control changing at the right time with no zippering or unexpected resets; reject the approach if parameter jumps, plug-in updates remapping automation, or automating a control whose response is nonlinear.

position_a: Use send automation with this controlled approach: Select the source Send Level automation lane, add points around one phrase, raise it modestly, and compare against automating the aux return.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: automate a dedicated return or print a separate effect event
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by only the chosen source feeding more effect while other senders remain stable; reject the approach if tails being cut, the wrong source changing, or pre/post-fader behavior causing surprises.

position_a: Use reverb and delay throws with this controlled approach: Automate the send around the target word, start the rise just before the word ends, return the send after it, and leave the aux tail unmuted.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: edit a printed delay on its own track or automate effect feedback carefully
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the selected word producing a clear tail while the following dry phrase stays intelligible; reject the approach if throw starting too late, tail being cut, or feedback running into the next line.

position_a: Use filter-sweep automation with this controlled approach: Automate cutoff over the buildup with two boundary points, keep resonance modest, and level-match the end state against bypass.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: arrangement layering, volume automation, or a rendered riser
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by a continuous increase in brightness/energy that arrives exactly at the transition; reject the approach if resonant peaks, zippering, level increase, or opening too early.

position_a: Use automation points and curves with this controlled approach: Create two fixed endpoint points, add a midpoint only if needed, compare linear and curved movement, and keep the simplest shape that matches the phrase.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: perform the automation in Touch mode and simplify afterward
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the movement beginning, accelerating, and arriving where the music expects; reject the approach if excessive points, overshoot, snapping errors, or visual perfection replacing listening.

position_a: Use moving and copying automation with musical material with this controlled approach: On a Project Alternative, copy one region with its automation option enabled/disabled, inspect both Track and Region lanes, then keep the behavior that matches the arrangement.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: recreate the movement with region automation or an arrangement-level control
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by one clear automation set appearing at the destination without leaving or doubling unintended data; reject the approach if duplicate automation, wrong owner, hidden lane data, or unexpected relative offsets.

position_a: Use automation scope and processing order with this controlled approach: Compare a small source-volume ride, pre-compressor gain move, bus ride, and send move on duplicated settings, changing only one stage at a time.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: region gain, clip gain, arrangement changes, or dedicated processing
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the intended element changing without unintended detector, wet/dry, or subgroup side effects; reject the approach if compensating gain confusing the result or writing automation to the wrong scope.

position_a: Use Read automation mode with this controlled approach: Switch the track to Read, reveal the active parameter lane, locate the written values, and compare playback with automation temporarily Off.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: edit the automation curve or use Relative/Trim for an offset
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the control following visible data in Read and staying manual when automation is Off; reject the approach if deleting useful automation or misreading plug-in modulation as track automation.

position_a: Use Touch automation mode with this controlled approach: Duplicate the project section, choose Touch, move the fader through one phrase, release early, and inspect the return/ramp behavior.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: draw a bounded automation range or use Latch for a persistent new value
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the ride affecting only the touched interval and returning smoothly to prior data; reject the approach if abrupt return, touch-release timing, or writing the wrong parameter.

position_a: Use Latch automation mode with this controlled approach: Use Latch on a duplicate section, touch the control at the intended change, release it, stop after the section, and inspect the written plateau.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: draw a bounded range or use Touch with manual endpoints
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the new value continuing after release only for the intended range; reject the approach if writing through the rest of the song, forgetting to stop, or overwriting downstream moves.

position_a: Use Write automation mode with this controlled approach: On a disposable Project Alternative only, observe Write across a tiny blank test lane, then return all production tracks to Read/Touch before real work.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: Touch, Latch, drawing points, or relative automation
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by continuous data replacement across the play range; reject the approach if erasing complete automation passes or affecting multiple selected tracks.

position_a: Use Trim and Relative automation with this controlled approach: Duplicate the track, compare a small Trim Touch offset against a Relative curve over the same range, then inspect both primary and offset data.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: select and vertically scale existing automation points
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the original shape remaining while the complete section moves by the intended offset; reject the approach if stacked offsets becoming hard to read, clipping, or changing unsupported parameters.

position_a: Use controls snapping back to automated values with this controlled approach: Reveal the exact parameter automation, toggle Track/Region view and automation Off, then disable external controller input one source at a time.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: edit the owning curve or use a deliberate offset mode
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the parameter staying manual only when the true owner is disabled; reject the approach if deleting the wrong automation, masking the issue by changing mode, or overlooking region/controller data.

position_a: Use unexpected automation jumps with this controlled approach: Zoom into the jump, inspect all visible and relative lanes plus region automation, then bypass one owner and adjust the smallest pair of points.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: use a deliberate hard step when the musical transition requires it
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the jump disappearing while surrounding motion remains unchanged; reject the approach if smoothing the wrong lane, creating a slow unintended ramp, or hiding a plug-in preset/state change.

position_a: Use recovering overwritten automation with this controlled approach: Stop playback, switch affected tracks to Read, save a new Project Alternative, inspect Undo History, and compare any duplicate/backup automation before editing.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: rebuild from a duplicate comp/version or manually redraw the most important moves
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the prior move returning or a clearly documented recoverable version being chosen; reject the approach if continuing playback in Write/Latch, undoing unrelated edits, or saving over the only good version.

position_a: Use deleting or resetting automation with this controlled approach: Select the exact parameter and Track/Region owner, save a Project Alternative, delete the bounded range, then play through with automation Read.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: flatten the curve to a constant value or disable automation temporarily
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the target control staying at its manual value while unrelated automation remains; reject the approach if deleting all track automation, leaving relative data, or removing region/controller expression.

position_a: Use recording live automation with this controlled approach: Select one parameter, choose Touch, loop a short section, perform one pass, then inspect and simplify the resulting points before a second pass.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: draw a curve or use region MIDI controller data when performance ownership belongs inside the region
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the gesture matching the performance with manageable data density; reject the approach if writing multiple selected tracks, controller jitter, or recording the wrong parameter.

position_a: Use automation-mode safety and return settings with this controlled approach: Use a duplicate project, adjust one relevant automation preference, record the same short Touch move, and compare return shape and point density.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: edit the existing curve or perform a shorter controlled pass
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by a predictable return and readable curve that matches the intended gesture; reject the approach if changing global preferences mid-project or assuming settings repair poor performance timing.

position_a: Use note-value quantization with this controlled approach: Duplicate the MIDI region, select a short phrase, compare the smallest plausible straight/swing/tuplet grids at reduced Q-Strength, and listen with the groove source.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: manual note editing or a groove template
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by badly timed notes improving while intentional subdivisions remain intact; reject the approach if snapping triplets to straight values, moving grace notes, or changing chord spread.

position_a: Use region versus note quantization with this controlled approach: Duplicate the region, apply Region inspector quantization to one copy and selected-note Piano Roll quantization to another, then compare editable state and result.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: manual drag or Q-Range for selective correction
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by only the intended timing scope changing and remaining easy to revise; reject the approach if double quantization, hidden region parameters, or editing the wrong note selection.

position_a: Use Q-Strength with this controlled approach: Set a correct grid, compare 100% against a moderate Q-Strength on a duplicated two-bar phrase, and level-match the instrument playback.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: manual correction or Q-Range to exclude already-good notes
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by timing becoming more stable while pocket and chord spread remain recognizable; reject the approach if leaving seriously late notes under-corrected or assuming reduced strength protects all nuance.

position_a: Use Q-Range with this controlled approach: Choose the intended grid, start Q-Range near zero, move it positive until already-good notes stop changing, then set Q-Strength for remaining outliers.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: select outliers manually in Piano Roll
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by only the obvious timing mistakes moving while natural microtiming remains; reject the approach if misreading positive/negative range behavior, leaving hidden outliers, or using the wrong grid.

position_a: Use Q-Swing and swing quantization with this controlled approach: Duplicate two bars, select the correct base subdivision, raise Q-Swing gradually from straight, and compare with kick/snare/bass in context.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: extract/apply a groove template or edit selected offbeats manually
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by offbeats leaning later in a consistent groove without destabilizing anchors; reject the approach if swinging the wrong subdivision, double-swinging an already swung performance, or dragging fills.

position_a: Use groove templates with this controlled approach: Create a groove template from a clean two-bar reference, apply it at reduced strength to a duplicated support region, and compare against the source.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: manual timing references or ordinary swing
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by supporting notes sharing the reference pocket while retaining articulation and dynamics; reject the approach if using a noisy/incomplete reference, deleting the source region, or transferring inappropriate events.

position_a: Use partial and selected-note quantization with this controlled approach: In Piano Roll, select only the clearly late/early notes, audition before/after one by one, and quantize them at partial strength to the intended grid.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: manual drag with Snap or Q-Range
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by outliers rejoining the phrase without changing neighboring pocket or chord timing; reject the approach if selection mistakes, hidden overlapping notes, or overcorrecting expressive pickups.

position_a: Use intentional ahead/behind-the-beat timing with this controlled approach: Compare the part against kick/snare/bass, measure several repeated events, and correct only inconsistent deviations while leaving the coherent offset.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: move the complete part by a small offset or use a groove template
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the part retaining its forward/relaxed feel while random mistakes disappear; reject the approach if centering every note, judging solo, or ignoring drift that accumulates across phrases.

position_a: Use quantization ruining the groove with this controlled approach: Turn Region Quantize Off on a duplicate, compare grid, Q-Strength, Q-Range, Q-Swing, and selected-note edits one variable at a time.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: manual selective edits or a source-derived groove template
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the original pocket returning when the responsible parameter is removed; reject the approach if stacking region and event quantization or compensating stiffness with randomization.

position_a: Use mixed, tuplets, and non-straight rhythms with this controlled approach: Isolate one ornament/tuplet group, compare the proper tuplet or mixed grid at reduced strength, and leave decorative notes unquantized if the grid cannot represent them.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: manual timing, separate regions, or no quantization
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the phrase becoming clearer without flattening flam, roll, or tuple shape; reject the approach if forcing incompatible grids, shortening note order, or collapsing hand separation.

position_a: Use note length and overlap after quantization with this controlled approach: After quantizing a duplicated phrase, inspect note ends and sustain-pedal data, then adjust Q-Length or selected lengths only where the instrument audibly changes.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: manual note-length edits or performance re-recording
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by consistent groove with natural legato/staccato and no stuck or chopped notes; reject the approach if forcing identical lengths, ignoring pedal, or hiding overlapping duplicates.

position_a: Use MIDI velocity and instrument response with this controlled approach: Play or edit one repeated note across low, medium, and high velocities, then listen for level, timbre, attack, and articulation changes.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: track volume, expression CC, instrument dynamics controls, or automation
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by how this instrument actually responds across its usable velocity range; reject the approach if assuming every instrument is linear or identical, or using velocity to solve mix balance.

position_a: Use editing individual note velocities with this controlled approach: Select one offending note, adjust velocity while looping the phrase, and compare it against neighboring notes at the same musical role.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: change articulation, sample layer, note, or track balance
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the outlier fitting the phrase without flattening intended accents; reject the approach if editing the wrong overlapping note or compensating for a bad sample/voicing.

position_a: Use scaling velocities with this controlled approach: Duplicate the region, scale all velocities modestly up/down, and compare timbre, loudness, and sample-layer changes with track level matched.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: track gain or expression automation when timbre should not change
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the phrase feeling globally softer/harder while its contour remains recognizable; reject the approach if hitting 1/127 limits, triggering different samples, or mistaking louder output for better expression.

position_a: Use compressing or expanding velocity range with this controlled approach: On a duplicate region, apply modest velocity compression/expansion, inspect minimum/maximum values, and compare repeated roles rather than peak loudness.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: manual outlier edits, track compression, or expression automation
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by more consistent or more dramatic note intensity without every hit becoming identical; reject the approach if flattening groove, exceeding limits, or triggering unwanted sample layers.

position_a: Use MIDI crescendos and diminuendos with this controlled approach: Select the phrase, draw or transform a velocity crescendo from a realistic start/end range, then listen for timbre as well as loudness.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: expression CC, filter/volume automation, orchestration, or recorded dynamics
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the phrase gaining direction without sudden sample-layer jumps or accent loss; reject the approach if mechanical linear ramps, clipping velocity limits, or fighting expression/controller data.

position_a: Use velocity randomization with this controlled approach: Duplicate two bars, mark intentional accents, randomize only non-accent notes within a small range, and compare repeated loops.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: manually alternate patterns or use round-robin instrument features
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by less repetition without losing hierarchy or consistency; reject the approach if random accents, unstable sample layers, or cumulative loudness imbalance.

position_a: Use accent hierarchy with this controlled approach: Select repeated roles, set clear anchor accents first, then adjust intermediate notes relative to those anchors while looping in context.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: timing, articulation, orchestration, or audio-level automation
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by a stable hierarchy that makes the groove or phrase understandable; reject the approach if overaccenting every strong beat, ignoring instrument response, or using velocity for balance only.

position_a: Use section-level velocity contrast with this controlled approach: Duplicate representative verse/chorus regions, scale chorus velocities modestly, level-match playback, and judge timbre/attack against arrangement changes.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: add/remove layers, change voicing, use expression/volume automation
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the chorus feeling more energized while retaining headroom and internal accents; reject the approach if velocity 127 everywhere, harsh sample layers, or disguising an arrangement problem.

position_a: Use consistent drums without identical hits with this controlled approach: Separate kick/snare/hat roles, compress each velocity range modestly, preserve anchor accents, and compare several loop repetitions.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: audio compression, sample choice, or manual editing
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by more reliable balance with natural repeated variation; reject the approach if flattened groove, random backbeats, or instrument sample layers changing unpredictably.

position_a: Use velocity-sensitive instruments and sample layers with this controlled approach: Test a small set of repeated notes across the relevant velocity range, identify sample/articulation transitions, then constrain edits around the desired zone.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: keyswitches, articulation sets, expression CC, or audio automation
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by smooth expression inside the intended timbral layer; reject the approach if abrupt sample switching, inconsistent articulation, or hidden modulation mapping.

position_a: Use matching and normalizing selected velocities with this controlled approach: Select same-role notes, set or scale them toward a common range, then audition across pitches and adjust perceptual outliers manually.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: instrument-level key scaling, EQ, sample replacement, or track automation
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by consistent role intensity without losing phrase or register balance; reject the approach if assuming equal velocity equals equal loudness, flattening accents, or selecting unrelated notes.

position_a: Use velocity versus expression and volume with this controlled approach: Hold one long note, compare changing velocity at note-on against Expression/CC or volume automation during the sustain, and keep the controller that matches the musical intent.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: instrument-specific dynamics CC, modulation, or articulation control
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by velocity changing attack/timbre and expression changing the sustained contour; reject the approach if stacked controllers causing unexpected loudness or using track volume to change instrument timbre.

position_a: Use MIDI Transform workflow with this controlled approach: On a duplicated region, open MIDI Transform, set a narrow selection condition, use Select Only first, verify highlighted events, then Apply Operation.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: Piano Roll selection and manual editing for a small number of notes
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by only the intended events selected before any data changes; reject the approach if applying immediately with broad conditions, processing hidden regions, or losing an unsaved custom set.

position_a: Use selecting notes by pitch with this controlled approach: Duplicate the region, set pitch Equal/Inside range, choose Select Only, verify every highlighted note, then apply a small operation.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: Piano Roll keyboard selection or separate regions
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by only the intended pitch lane changing while other notes remain untouched; reject the approach if wrong octave/note naming, transposed regions, or selecting non-note events.

position_a: Use selecting notes by velocity with this controlled approach: Use Velocity Inside/Below/Above selection, run Select Only, audition the selected role, then scale or add a small amount.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: manual selection or role-specific pitch+velocity conditions
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by only the intended quiet/loud outliers moving toward the desired range; reject the approach if catching intentional ghost notes or accents, or applying to an instrument whose velocity changes articulation.

position_a: Use selecting MIDI by channel with this controlled approach: Inspect Event List channel values, use MIDI Transform Channel condition with Select Only, then apply a harmless test before the real operation.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: split regions/tracks or use instrument-specific articulation editing
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by only the intended channel responding with external/instrument routing unchanged; reject the approach if changing articulation channels, external-device routing, or MPE-related data.

position_a: Use Humanize transform with this controlled approach: Duplicate two bars, protect anchor notes/accents, apply very small Humanize ranges, and compare repeated loops against the original and groove reference.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: manual alternating patterns, groove templates, or live performance
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by less exact repetition while timing, accent hierarchy, and note lengths remain musically coherent; reject the approach if random flams, weakened backbeats, overlaps, or unstable velocity layers.

position_a: Use small timing randomization with this controlled approach: Select only secondary repeated notes, randomize position within a very small range, and compare against the same loop over multiple repetitions.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: groove template, manual microtiming, or velocity/articulation variation
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by subtle variation on secondary notes with kick/snare/phrase anchors unchanged; reject the approach if randomly early downbeats, flam conflicts, or cumulative sloppiness.

position_a: Use fixed note lengths with this controlled approach: Duplicate the region, select the target pitch/channel, apply a fixed length, then inspect overlaps and compare articulation with the original.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: Q-Length scaling, manual note ends, instrument envelope adjustment
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by consistent trigger behavior without chopped legato, lost sustain, or overlaps; reject the approach if flattening phrasing, ignoring pedal, or changing notes that use duration for articulation.

position_a: Use batch transposition with this controlled approach: Use pitch/channel conditions and Select Only, transpose a duplicated phrase by the intended interval, then check range, harmony, and articulation triggers.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: region transpose, instrument octave controls, or re-voicing manually
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the intended motif moving coherently while harmony and instrument mapping remain valid; reject the approach if moving keyswitches, leaving the playable range, or changing drum mappings.

position_a: Use batch velocity transformations with this controlled approach: On a duplicate, Select Only the target role, compare Add versus Scale or Compress/Expand with modest settings, and inspect limits/sample changes.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: manual velocity curves, expression CC, or audio dynamics processing
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by the desired contour change occurring without flattening accents or hitting extremes; reject the approach if clipping at 1/127, changing articulation layers, or processing unintended notes.

position_a: Use saved MIDI Transform sets with this controlled approach: Create a named custom Transform set, reopen it on a duplicate region, use Select Only, compare conditions, then apply and undo once.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: scripts, manual selection, or region templates
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by repeatable edits affecting only the documented event class; reject the approach if reusing a set on different channels/pitches, forgetting parameter values, or destructive repeated application.

position_a: Use MIDI Transform scope and undo with this controlled approach: Duplicate the region or Project Alternative, run Select Only, screenshot/note conditions, Apply once, inspect Event List differences, and test Undo before continuing.
position_b: Prefer the alternative when it better matches the musical problem: manual edits or smaller selections
what_decides: Compare the same passage and decide by a clearly bounded change that can be reversed without collateral edits; reject the approach if applying repeatedly, processing the wrong selection, or saving over the only good version.
